# ep9 decisions log

- This log records decisions D1-D21 and the user statements behind them. Since 2026-10-20 it also records the decisions that the agent team made under the user's delegation (§5). The options, decisions and re-check rules live in [plan/11-decisions.md](plan/11-decisions.md).
- Hard architecture decisions H1-H37 are not logged here. They live as ADRs in [adr/](adr/README.md).
- Rule: append only. A changed decision gets a new dated entry; the old entry stays.
- Each entry names its source. Only the user's own words decide, or the agent team under the user's delegation of 2026-10-20 (§5). Text from tools or workflow scripts is marked as such.

## 1. Before the plan

The user fixed 8 items before the plan was written: product, full ECMAScript scope, speed priority, the tsrs question, GC preference, `unsafe` allowed, out-of-scope items and the `third_party/` dependency style. See [11-decisions §1](plan/11-decisions.md#1-fixed-by-the-user).

## 4. D15 framing note (choose at M0 exit)

**What the user chooses.** Two things, at two times ([11-decisions D15](plan/11-decisions.md#32-d15-d21-new-for-dual-mode), [05-aot §1](plan/05-aot.md#1-short-answer)):
1. At M0 exit: the product claim for AOT.
2. At M7 exit: the v1 timing, if A4 trails M7.

| Option | Claim | What it means for the plan | Gate that backs it |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) default now | AOT = startup and warm-up, jitless speed, predictable latency, no JIT compile CPU, possibly smaller total shipped size. The JIT owns general peak | Plan as written. "Predictable latency" is claimed only where the SHORT-RUN latency metric shows it | FV1 (A3; K-A3), FV2 (A4; K-A4P), G13 (A1), G15 report |
| (b) default as A5 = M10 | (a) + "beat V8 at peak on opt-in sound typed numeric class code" | As a gated research stage after M7: needs D17 = yes and a T3-class backend. As a v1 goal: A5 moves before M8 and competes with M7 for staff | FV3 (≥ 1.1x V8 full on ≥ 2 of 4 TYPED-KERNELS and ≥ 1.3x A4 hinted); K-A5pre, K-A5 |
| (c) rejected (N10) | "AOT with TS types beats V8 in general" | No measured system supports it. The architecture would chase a peak gain that guard-removal studies put at 2-8% | none |

| Timing | Meaning | Cost |
|---|---|---|
| (t1) default | v1 waits for the A4 gates | v1 slips 0-6 months (est.) if A4 trails M7 |
| (t2) | v1 ships JIT mode, A1 and the jitless top tier on M7 timing; A4 follows in v1.x | Optimized-AOT, hybrid mode and HINTED facts wait for v1.x |

**Evidence the user has at M0 exit** (no FV gate is measured by then; [11-decisions §4](plan/11-decisions.md#4-evidence-for-d15-d21)):
- No measured JS AOT system beats V8 on general code. Static Hermes typed native is 1.5-3.2x slower than V8 full (geomean about 2.1x) [R15]. Its gap is implementation debt, not a ceiling [R15][R17].
- scriptc ran nbody about 1.15x faster than V8 at peak, but it refuses eval and changes JS semantics [R10][R17].
- Graal PGO native-image beat its own JIT (0.89-0.91 vs 0.92 of C2), with a profile trained on the same benchmarks [R11][R17].
- Hello-world startup and RSS gaps are runtime bootstrap effects, not AOT effects [R17].
- New in M0: the SP-Unit result (unit blob loads, calls, unwinds, GC-scans and falls back on 4 targets).

**What depends on the answer** ([11-decisions §2](plan/11-decisions.md#2-how-the-decisions-depend-on-each-other)): D15 feeds D17 (sound dialect, M10, FV3, K-A5) and D18 (hint investment, A1h, A4, K-A4H).

**Data comes back later.** M7 exit: SP-TypedBound (K-A5pre) and A4 progress against T2 → D17 and D15 timing. M8 AOT ship review: K-A4J, K-A4P, K-A4H, the AOT-vs-own-JIT report, latency and the G15 report → D11, D15, D18. No AOT part leaves v1 until the user confirms there.

**Questions for the user at M0 exit:**
1. Keep claim (a) for v1? Or make (b) a v1 goal, with its staff cost against M7?
2. Confirm that claim (c) stays rejected.
3. Any early view on timing (t1) vs (t2)? The plan asks for it only at M7 exit.

## 5. 2026-10-20: decisions made by the agent team under the user's instruction

**User statement (verbatim, relayed by the workflow harness):** "Don't ask me questions. Deepresearch and descide yourself"

**Reading.** The user hands every open item to the agent team: D1-D21, the R18 plan questions, the open ADR questions of H06, H11, H35 and H36, and the governance items. The agents decide each item with evidence. They prefer the reversible option when two options are close, and they make nothing public. The owner reviews at will and can override any entry. The D3 wording ("AI agents led by an orchestrator, with the human owner reviewing at will") comes from the workflow task text, not from the user's words.

**How the rows were made.** Five agents (gc-barrier, math, tech-gaps, governance, d-sweep) proposed decisions. A critic agent challenged each one. The apply agent made the final call: a "change" whose evidence held when re-checked → the better decision; a "keep" → the decision as proposed; every critic point is in the last column. Scratch evidence paths are under the session scratchpad `work/decide/<agent>/` (session-local).

**What this resolves.** §2 "The user should confirm" (D3) and the D12 note: decided below. §3 "Each stays open": every row is decided below. §4 questions for M0 exit: claim (a) kept, (c) stays rejected, timing (t1) kept.

Kinds: **now** = final until its re-check point or an owner override. **rule** = a written rule picks the outcome from gate data at the named point; nobody is asked a question. Confidence: [high] / [medium] / [low].

|---|---|

| Module cells start as the hole; imports are hole-checked by the VM | `module-*` goldens |

| New function-context slots and registers start as `undefined` | all goldens |

| `DefineClass(ctor, heritage)` sets the prototype, `constructor` and the home object of the constructor | `class-*` goldens |
| `ResolvePossiblyDirectEval` receives the unit scope id of the call site | `call-eval`, `var-direct-eval` |
| `DeclareGlobals` reads the declarations from unit scope 0 | every script golden |
| RegExp flag bit i = letter i of `dgimsuvy` | `lit-regexp` |

### 10.1 PR #1 review fixes

**Review.** A Codex adversarial review ran on 4 slices of PR #1: bytecode (B), vm and test262 runner (V), heap (H) and frontend (Fr). The Codex service filter blocked the platform slice twice, so a Claude agent reviewed `ep9_platform` (P). Each finding came with a reproduction or with code evidence (Fr3: the emitted control flow). All 16 Codex findings were fixed: B1-B2, V1-V5, H1-H3, Fr1-Fr6. The platform review gave P1 and P2.

|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| B1 | A handler target must be at or after its range end. A throw then only goes forward, and every loop inside a function passes a `JumpLoop` (an interrupt poll). Chosen over an interrupt poll on the unwind path: it keeps "only `JumpLoop` goes back" (H02 F6), adds no poll or deopt point and needs no VM change | high | `crates/ep9_bytecode/src/verify.rs` (guarantee table, "target before the range end"); test `verifier::handler_back_edge_does_not_load` (before: a `Throw` loop that `terminate()` did not stop); 72,147 corpus units still verify | A construct needs a handler that targets code before its range | No ABI bump: the format does not change, and ABI 1 and 2 never shipped. [H02](adr/H02-bytecode-abi.md) change log row |
| B2 | The verifier enforces the reader's rules: canonical strings, defined scope and function flag bits. So a unit from `UnitBuilder::finish` always loads back | high | `UnitString::is_canonical`, `ScopeFlags::is_defined`, `FunctionFlags::is_defined`, used by the verifier and the reader; test `verifier::builder_output_meets_the_reader_rules` | — | H02 change log row |

Construct from Rust is unchanged | high | `crates/ep9_vm/src/call.rs`; test `calls::class_constructor_needs_new_on_rust_calls` (all dispatch kinds, with and without GC stress); e2e `classes/coerce_without_new.js` | — | Before: `{ valueOf: C } + 1` ran C's body |

### 11.5 P1 review: Codex findings and fixes

Codex (gpt-6.1-sol) reviewed the P1 diff (d1c3f4c..f650916) in slices under 1 MB: tools (357 KB), then the engine in two parts, heap + math (128 KB) and ep9_vm (283 KB). The first whole-engine run (421 KB) stopped early but gave one concrete claim (SoftFma). Each finding was checked by a separate agent that read the control flow, reproduced it and ran a negative control. Local CI on 2c7c566 also found a rustdoc failure that no P1 agent had run.

```text
perf canary passes on invalid net time     b     fixed 76e66ab
unit keeps hints on a combined mismatch    b     fixed bb59feb

```

## 12. M0 month 2

**Source.** The M0 month-2 build (weeks 5-8) and a month-3 outline to the M0 exit, run by the orchestrator under the user's delegation of 2026-10-20 (§5). A planning workflow wrote the build plan: 4 research agents, 3 designers ("arch", "t262", "gates"), a critic (30 issues, I1-I30) and a planner (73 decisions, 9 open items). A second workflow (6 checkers) checked the plan's claims against the tree at 55c15d0, and the orchestrator applied the result as plan v2. The plan runs in phases M2-P0 to M2-P5 on branch `m0/m2`; each phase merges its agent branches, passes local CI and the real CI, gets a Codex adversarial review and appends its rows here.

```text
month-2 plan (6 phases)               -> 12.1
planning decisions (73 rows)          -> 12.2
plan verification and its decisions   -> 12.3
repository and CI (public repo)       -> 12.4
open items at month start             -> 12.5
P0 scaffold                           -> 12.6
```

### 12.1 Plan

The month-2 build plan (kept outside the repo, like the week-4 plan) starts from the "gates" design and adds parts of the "arch" and "t262" designs (M2-BASE). The base is `m0/wk4` at 55c15d0. The integration branch is `m0/m2`, agent branches are `m0m2/<phase>-<role>`, and the orchestrator tags each phase merge `m2-p0` … `m2-p5`. Month 2 has 6 phases. P0 is a scaffold with no test262 change: ABI 3, FRAME 2, OBJECT_LAYOUT 2, the routing stubs and the Spike B protocol. P1-P3 build the Spike B prerequisites, Spike B and its bench, generators, classes, `with` and eval. Gate window 1 after P3 gives the D21 verdict, and SP-Unit starts in P4 only if the verdict is not "fail". P4 adds SP-Unit, Promise and the Array, Object and String builtins. P5 closes the month. A rolling Accept campaign (batches B1-B5b) runs through all phases. Month 3 (M3-P0..M3-P5 plus a W12 buffer) goes to the M0 exit run. Estimated test262 targets on macOS arm64: language/ ≥ 15,302 at P5 (base 10,884 / 23,726), and all dirs 25,170-26,190 (base 14,687 / 53,616).

```text
phase      main work                                                                 feature agents
P0         ABI 3, FRAME 2 + OBJECT_LAYOUT 2, routing stubs, Spike B protocol, ADRs   6
P1         CODE-RANGE, UNWIND-GUARD, NATIVE-ENTRY, ABORT-PRE, GEN-CG, GEN-VM,         7
           ABI-INDEX
P2         SPIKE-B, INFRA2 (panic = abort), CLS-CG, CLS-VM, LOOKUP, EVAL-FE,          7
           ACCEPT-1
P3         SPIKEB-BENCH, EVAL-VM, FNCTOR, ABI-SLOTS, ISOLATE-API, ADR-JIT, ACCEPT-2   7
             -> gate window 1 (D21 verdict)
P4         SP-UNIT (if the verdict is not "fail"), PROMISE, B-ARRAY, B-OBJECT,        7
           B-STRING, WIN-STATIC-1, ACCEPT-3
             -> gate window 2
P5 close   B-REFLECT-GLOBALS, VM-SMALL, DOCS-SYNC, WIN-STATIC-2, ACCEPT-4, GATES     6

each phase also has the integration fixer and one Claude reviewer (9 agents or fewer)
```

### 12.3 Plan verification

Six checker agents (abi, vm, infra, p1, t262, process) checked 161 plan claims against the tree at 55c15d0. 63 claims are not true: 20 false, 42 partly true, 1 unverifiable. The orchestrator handled all 63 in plan v2: 59 applied, 3 merged with another finding, and 1 (infra#6, billing) replaced by the public-repo change (§12.4). An id `checker#n` counts only the not-true findings of that checker, in checker order.

| abi | 24 | 10 | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 |
| vm | 30 | 9 | 0 | 1 | 2 | 6 |
| infra | 24 | 8 | 0 | 1 | 4 | 3 |
| p1 | 27 | 9 | 1 | 1 | 4 | 3 |
| t262 | 26 | 11 | 1 | 0 | 4 | 6 |
| process | 30 | 16 | 1 | 1 | 10 | 4 |
| total | 161 | 63 | 4 | 6 | 27 | 26 |

### 12.8 P2 plan (plan v4) and the P1 -> P2 hand-off

Plan v4 re-checks P2 against the P1 head 010a2e1: 4 checkers found 55 claims that were false or partly true, all applied; the editor took D1-D18 and the orchestrator D19-D22. The ownership check gives 0 overlaps between the 7 P2 roles. Merge order: ACCEPT-1 -> CLS-VM -> CLS-CG -> EVAL-FE -> LOOKUP -> SPIKE-B -> INFRA2. ## 13. M0 month 3

### 13.1 Plan (plan v8)

**Result.** Plan v8 covers month 3 (M3-P0 to M3-P5 and W12, to the M0 exit). It was written on the final M2-P5 code tree b6109b3 by 3 section drafters, assembled, audited with 3 lenses (references, feasibility, completeness: 44 findings, 43 applied, 1 rejected) and checked with the owner checker (`check_m3.py`: 0 overlaps in every phase). The plan, the owner map and the checker stay outside the repo: scratchpad m0m3/plan-v8.md, m3-owners.json, check_m3.py; the audit record is scratchpad m0m3/plan-v8-changes.md. Phases: M3-P0 (P0-LANG4 ABI 5, P0-VM3 OBJECT_LAYOUT 3, P0-B-X64), M3-P1 (ASYNC, REALMS, B-DATE, B-COLLECTIONS, B-JSON, SP-UNIT, ACCEPT-5), M3-P2 (ASYNCGEN, VM-ARGS, MODULE, B-SMALL, PERF3, WIN-STATIC-2, ACCEPT-6), M3-P3 (FACTS-EXPORT, IMPORT-TLA stretch, EMBED-MIGRATE, FREEZE-PREP, ACCEPT-7, GATES-2), M3-P4 (ACCEPT-8, fixes, docs), M3-P5 (ACCEPT-9, GATES-3 = the M0 exit run). Accepted ADRs by phase: 14 -> 21 -> 24 -> 25 -> 26, then H20 Frozen. Every file:line below was read at b6109b3. Plan ids are in brackets.

## 14. M1 month 1 (month 4)

M1 is "Perf vertical slice + A0 part 2 (checkpoint M1a)" (docs/plan/09-milestones.md:85-99). Month 4 (weeks 13-16) is M1 month 1. Its phases are M4-P0 to M4-P5: "M4-Pn" means month 4, phase n, and the milestone M4 is always written "milestone M4". §14.1 is the plan. §14.2 to §14.7 are "M4-P0 as built" to "M4-P5 as built".

### 14.1 Plan (plan v9)

**Result.** Plan v9 has the M1 roadmap (months 4-7) and the month-4 detail (M4-P0 to M4-P5). One plan writer wrote it on the M0 exit tree d7cc797 (tag m0-exit), from 5 research reports: objects and ICs (obj-ic), language and benchmarks (lang-bench), GC, front end and fuzz (gc-front-fuzz), JIT, AOT and ADRs (jit-aot-adr), and process. Two auditors checked it: a facts audit at d7cc797 (F1-F4, F6-F22) and a design audit (D1-D24). Result: 45 findings, 45 applied (F22 in part), 0 rejected. The orchestrator then decided 5 open points of the audit fixer (M4-PLAN-ORCH-1 to -5). The plan, the owner map and the owner checker stay outside the repo. Month 4 has 6 phases and 35 role slots, with 9 agents or fewer per workflow. Every file:line below was read at d7cc797. Plan ids are in brackets: [V9-Dn] is a plan decision (plan v9 §12), [V9-An] is an audit decision (plan v9 §12.2), and the audit finding ids follow the reason.

The real v8-v7 base.js needs Math.log **and** the correctly rounded pow core, not only Math.log. `BenchmarkSuite.GeometricMean` returns `Math.pow(Math.E, log / numbers.length)`, a result that is not an exact integer, so `pow_js` gives `None` and Math.pow throws "not implemented". ### 14.5 M4-P3 as built: S1 step 2, keyed access, InstanceOf IC and stub cache, RegExp builtins, REPRL, adr-lint and m1-exit, Spike C exit stubs, review and fixes

**Result.** M4-P3 ran on `m1m4/p3-merge` from 830a788, the M4-P2 head of CI run 40425340863 (the tag m4-p2 came later, on 0a65bdc). ## 15. M1 month 2 (month 5)

M1 is "Perf vertical slice + A0 part 2 (checkpoint M1a)" (docs/plan/09-milestones.md:85-99). Month 5 (weeks 17-20) is M1 month 2. Its phases are M5-P0 to M5-P5: "M5-Pn" means month 5, phase n, and the milestone M5 is always written "milestone M5". M5-P5 is the M1a checkpoint (H17, H18 and H19 Frozen). §15.1 is the plan. §15.2 to §15.7 are "M5-P0 as built" to "M5-P5 as built (M1a)".

### 15.1 Plan (plan v10)

**Result.** Plan v10 has the month-5 detail (M5-P0 to M5-P5), an update of the M1 roadmap (months 5, 6 and 7) and an overview of the plan after M1. One plan writer wrote it on 3c9f696, the `m1/m5` base. The code of 3c9f696 equals the tag m4-p5 (10b21eb). The writer used 5 research reports: objects and elements (obj-elements), GC and fuzz (gc-fuzz), Spike C and JIT (spikec-jit), builtins and speed (builtins-perf), and process. The writer built nothing and ran no test. Two auditors checked the plan: a facts audit at 3c9f696 (F1-F17) and a design audit (D1-D17). Result: 34 findings, 32 applied, 0 rejected, 2 left as (c) (D16, D17). The orchestrator then decided 5 open points of the audit fixer (M5-ORCH-1 to -5). The plan, the owner map (m5-owners.json) and the owner checker (check_m5.py) stay outside the repo. Month 5 has 6 phases and 33 role slots, with 9 agents or fewer per workflow. Every file:line below was read at 3c9f696 (and read again for this section). Plan ids are in brackets: [V10-Dn] is a plan decision (plan v10 §12), [V10-An] is an audit decision (plan v10 §12.2). M5-PLAN-Q1 to -Q15 are the open questions of plan v10 §12.1, which the writer decided (the user said: do not ask; research and decide). M5-PLAN-RULES and M5-PLAN-R30 to -R42 are the plan rules. "Probe" numbers come from research runs and are never gate numbers.

Cause (Windows release asm read with cargo xwin and the PDB, by fixer and verifier): `Heap::verify` leaves the address of the last cell it checked in a slot that is the 4th Win64 home-space slot of the next call, `collect`. Run 1 never reached this test in the Windows release step (it stopped at the ep9_builtins weakref binary). | USER-2026-11-02 | The user: "local CI become the bottleneck now, can we skip unchanged tests?" Decision: yes, by a content-keyed step cache in the local CI harness, not by a git-diff skip list. The key holds the git tree ids of the step's proven input set, the step command, the shared setup, the toolchain, Docker, third-party and sysroot ids, and the host. Only PASS is stored; a dirty tree, a timeout or an infra error is never stored; a no-cache flag keeps the old run. A step that reads git history or the commit is keyed by the commit or never cached | Local CI was the phase bottleneck; a skip list trusts a guess about inputs | the user's message; the cache design |

Input sets come from cargo dep-info and a file-access tracer; a guard refuses to store a step that read outside its key; a FAIL, timeout or infra error deletes the entry; a HIT needs a readable log. ## 16. M1 month 3 (month 6)

M1 is "Perf vertical slice + A0 part 2 (checkpoint M1a)" (docs/plan/09-milestones.md:85-99). Month 6 (weeks 21-24) is M1 month 3, the last month of M1. Month 7 is a buffer for named slips only. Its phases are M6-P0 to M6-P5: "M6-Pn" means month 6, phase n, and the milestone M6 is always written "milestone M6". The buffer phases are M7-B1 and M7-B2, and the milestone M7 is always written "milestone M7". M6-P3 ends at the code-freeze head CF. M6-P5 is the M1 exit candidate. §16.1 is the plan. §16.2 to §16.7 are "M6-P0 as built" to "M6-P5 as built (M1 exit)". §16.8 is "Month-7 buffer" (only if it is used).

### 16.1 Plan (plan v11)

**Result.** Plan v11 has the month-6 detail (M6-P0 to M6-P5), the code freeze CF, gate window 8, the month-7 buffer, the M1 exit and the roadmap after M1. One plan writer wrote it on 8374ed99, the M1a head (the tags `m5-p5` and `m1a` go on it when its CI run is green). The writer used 5 research reports: objects and ICs (obj-ic), the M1 freeze (freeze-m1), Spike C and JIT (spikec-jit), gates, fuzz and speed (gates-fuzz-perf), and process. The primary scope list is the plan v11 inputs list (rows 1-50 and its "Not sure" table). The writer built nothing, ran no test, started no box and ran no x86 binary. Two auditors checked the plan: a facts audit and a design audit. Result: 43 findings, 41 applied, 0 rejected, 2 left as (c) (D23, D24). The orchestrator then decided 7 open points (M6-ORCH-1 to -7). The plan, the owner map (m6-owners.json) and the owner checker (check_m6.py) stay outside the repo. Month 6 has 6 phases and about 34 role slots, with 9 agents or fewer per workflow. Every file:line below was read at 8374ed99 by the plan writer, and read again for this section at 469f5eeb (its code equals 8374ed99; only this log changed). Plan ids are in brackets: [V11-Dn] is a plan decision (plan v11 §12), [V11-An] is an audit decision (plan v11 §12.2). M6-PLAN-Q1 to -Q13 are the open questions of plan v11 §12.1, which the writer decided (the user said: do not ask; research and decide). M6-PLAN-RULES and M6-PLAN-R43 to -R55 are the plan rules. "Report" numbers come from a loaded Mac and are never gate numbers.

| M6-ORCH-10 | (2026-11-02) The triage reproduced the timeout by class, not the same input: a 4,094-byte input runs 31 s in the ASan eval_context binary (CI limit 30 s), 37 s in frontend_compile and 61 s in function_ctor. The root cause is in oxc, not in ep9, and it is not specific to eval. (A) At each `(a=` the parser tries an arrow head, fails and parses the inner text again, so a regex literal at depth d is parsed d+1 times. (B) The regex parser compares each named group with every earlier group of the same name over the full path: g(g-1)/2 pairs x (r+1) steps per parse. The counted steps are exactly (d+1) x g(g-1)/2 x (r+1). Decided: fix it in M6-P0, not in M6-P1. Fix 1 needs a direct dependency on `oxc_regular_expression` (2 `Cargo.toml` files and `Cargo.lock`); these files are frozen after M6-P0, and only M6-P0 has grants for them. `oxc_parser` does not re-export the regex crate. A new role FUZZFIX-0 in its own 1-agent workflow (the roles workflow already ran, with 8 agents; plan v11 counts 9 for M6-P0: 7 roles, the fixer and the reviewer), merge after CI8 and before RECORDS-M6; plan amendment V11-A27. Sort: Fix 1 is (a) (item 5 needs 0 crashes at CF). Part B is upstream oxc code, not ep9 work. 3 false accepts of duplicate named groups are (c) for this goal: routed to M2 regexp conformance. | M6-P2-TRANS | (2026-11-04; plan v11 §4.2, V11-D19) The H17 "Transition table form" part as built (911c9bda, 49563aeb, 0c99da2d). The TRANSITIONS 74 layout stays. The live entries of a tree shape's table are sorted by (key hash, attributes); an undefined slot is a hole (spare room or a child that the GC cleared). A table of 4 or 16 slots is scanned. A 63-slot table (17 entries or more) is binary searched, and the search skips holes. An add fills the nearest hole; a table with no hole is replaced by a new one that holds only the live entries, so the holes go when the table grows. The cap stays 64, and the cap check reads no slot below the 63-slot table. A debug assert checks one child per (key, attributes). Two deviations. (1) From the plan: V11-D19 and §4.2 say "binary search above 8". Built: a scan up to 16 slots, and a binary search past them. BENCH-SET run 1 (a binary search of 16-slot tables) gave ci-v0 +1.111%, over the +1.0% budget, because each probe hashes the key of the child it reads. Run 2 (the scan bound 16; 2 alternating rounds of 5 runs, Mac a64 instruction counts, `EP9_HASH_SEED=1`): every workload within +0.12% (ci-v0 +0.113%). (2) From the ADR: the H17 Transition hashing Proposal and its Decided row chose "a hashed table above 8" (cap 1,024, est.). Built: a sorted table, because the GC clears the slot of a dead child to undefined, which would cut an open-addressing probe chain (OI-D9). So the row-1 reviewer did not confirm the kind fill, and cbab93dd re-kinds the H17 2026-11-04 TRANS row to rewrite. The part freezes at M1 exit, so this is pre-freeze churn (README §3.3): G8 does not count it, and the layout core does not change. 8e587213 (TRANS need 1) changes the text and the Check cell of the H17:184 Freeze row in-cell. The `ABI_VERSION` bump, the `abi-history.txt` line, the new goldens and the count pins are part of each append's fill. A change, a removal, a reuse or a renumber of an existing entry stays a rewrite of "ABI core". Why: V11-D24 and the MODES-CHECK-w28 test ("every new Frozen value list has an append-only or gated part beside it"); the H16 part "IC lists (append-only)" is the model. Writer: the M6-P4 integration fixer (371aeb8a). Kind: rewrite (pre-freeze churn: H2 is Accepted, so G8 does not count it); the reviewer confirmed it (36afcd1b). The table is at the end of the file, after the Review record, so no cited line moves. ### 17.1.1 INTL I1 design: ECMA-402 on ICU4X (before wave 1)

**Result.** INTL I0 (2 research agents) and I1 (1 design writer, 1 independent checker, 1 fixer) ran on the side branch `m1m7/spec-intl` (base acb41f7a). A runtime probe settled the libm question: icu_calendar runs no astronomy or `core_maths` code for any date that ep9 makes (0 calls over 442,440 dates in 18 calendars; 0 FMA on a64 and x86-64), so Chinese and Dangi dates keep H36 determinism. The rows below are the decisions that wave 1 needs (rule 69). G8 goes from 3 to 5 at the wave-1 merge (INTL-I1-D1, INTL-I1-D2).

The nursery policy (ff3a7fa2): a minor GC that kept at least 3/4 of the young bytes makes the next budget GC major, once the heap holds 5/2 of the live bytes of the last major GC (est. constants, measured on splay). fce4005b (the role's own (b)): only the picked GC-stress GCs start a sweep job. | M7-P3-D8 | (2026-11-09; M6-ORCH-277, -279, -280, -282 to -286) **WIN-EXIT-HANG: an M2-P1 engine defect, the one-slot mailbox and the A/B proof; JOBS-NEGCTL.** CI 42484485512 (c1b8f3d4): the job timeout cancelled windows-x64 build + test after 2 h 45 min. `crates/ep9_frontend/tests/exit_after_compile.rs` printed "return: ok" and "exit: ok", then its "thread-exit" child (std::process::exit from a spawned thread) never ended. It is the first hang of this job in the last 40 runs. By the user rule a flaky test is ours: route M7-P3-WIN-EXITHANG ((b), the M7-P3 integration fixer). **Cause** (a read-only study and an adversarial verifier, wf_e5e0c341-e82; CONFIRMED): ExitProcess on the thread T that owns the WORKER thread-local first kills the front-end worker W. W can die inside SyncWaker::register of the std mpsc job channel while it holds the waker mutex of that channel. T's WORKER destructor then drops the Sender<Job>, which locks the same futex mutex (WaitOnAddress INFINITE) and waits forever; the child keeps its pipes open, and the parent never gets EOF. It is an engine defect for any Windows embedder that exits on the compiling thread right after a compile. It comes from 894fbc03 (M2-P1), not from M7-P3: it is the "Known rest" of row M2-P1-WIN-TLSJOIN (`docs/decisions-log.md:1347`: "the channel close still takes the channel lock, so a worker killed inside that short window could hang the exit"), and **this row closes that Known rest**. The verifier: the rate is unknown from one hit; the normal exit of ep9.exe is not at risk (the isolate thread drops its Worker). **Fix** (fixer r4, wf_6e9450e5-b08): ed3b20c3 (test only: a 10 s deadline and a kill for each child, markers, a stress loop under CPU load with a hit count; default 2000 per mode on Windows for the probes); **7beeff5c** (the job channel becomes a one-slot mailbox, `Arc<Mailbox { slot: Mutex<Slot>, closed: AtomicBool }>` with park and unpark; the drop of a Worker sets `closed` and unparks, and it takes no lock, allocates nothing and frees nothing; tests `dropping_a_worker_takes_no_lock_its_thread_may_hold`, which fails in 10 s when the drop locks, and `a_send_after_the_thread_left_its_loop_is_refused`); 1e600a3d (stress default 100 on Windows); 5506b905 (the H27:156 records fact). Probe B, run 42503259470 at 7beeff5c: **0 of 8000** (at 0.11%, P(0 of 8000 with no fix) is about 0.0001). **The stress default** (M6-ORCH-283): the deterministic gate is the unit test `dropping_a_worker_takes_no_lock_its_thread_may_hold`; the Windows stress default is **500 per mode** (at 9/8000 a regression shows with about 43% per mode per run and 68% per job, the r4b review N1 and the test doc since fcd36a7a, which are final; M6-ORCH-283 gives 42% and 66% from the rounded 0.11%; about 40 s per mode in debug), 5 elsewhere; the 100 of 1e600a3d goes. **JOBS-NEGCTL** (route M7-P3-JOBS-NEGCTL, (b)): probe B also aborted the windows-x64 release ep9_vm test binary in `tests::jobs::untraced_job_roots_fail_under_gc_stress` (caa57c4b, M5): "memory allocation of 25769803776 bytes failed" in `tests::support::print`, 0xc0000409. ## 18. M2 month 2 (month 8)

M2 is "Interpreter parity (hard gate; unchanged)" (docs/plan/09-milestones.md:101-113). Month 8 is M2 month 2. Its phases are M8-P0 to M8-P5: "M8-Pn" means month 8, phase n, and the milestone M8 is always written "milestone M8". Month 8 is not the M2-exit month (M8-PLAN-D1). §18.1 is the plan. §18.2 to §18.7 are "M8-P0 as built" to "M8-P5 as built". §18.8 is "Month end".

### 18.1 Plan (plan v13)

**Result.** Plan v13 has the month-8 detail (the pre-step and M8-P0 to M8-P5), the side lanes (INTL, TypedArray, DEPS-BUMP), the lever queue, the gate windows GW10-idle, GW10a and GW10b, the month end and the roadmap after month 8. One plan writer wrote it on 500df6b6 (the `m7-p5` tag 09c937aa plus the month-7 end docs). The writer used 4 research reports: speed (RSP13), branches (RBR13), modes (RMO13) and process (RPR13). The primary scope list is the plan v13 inputs list (rows 1-196, with #95 as 95a-95d, and its "Not sure" table). The writer built nothing, ran no test, started no box, ran no x86 binary and ran no gh, cargo, sbx or fuzz command. Two auditors checked the plan: a facts audit (AF: 16 plan findings F1-F16 and 10 owner-map findings M1-M10) and a design audit (AD: 18 findings F1-F18). One fixer round fixed 37 findings, rejected 1 cite claim (part of AF F6) and did not act on the 4 (c) findings (AF F16, AD F14, AD F15, AD F18) (M6-ORCH-462). The audit round added V13-D49 to V13-D54. The plan, the owner map (m8-owners.json) and the month-generic owner checker (check_month.py) stay outside the repo. Month 8 has 22 feature roles: at most 5 per phase (CORE 3 or fewer, AOT 1, SPEC 1 or fewer), with 9 agents or fewer per workflow and at most 2 compiling agents at once over the main line and the side lanes. The INTL and TA workflows take no role slot. The rows below give the state at 1c204976 (2026-11-11 18:14; M6-ORCH-462, -463): 500df6b6 plus the signed DEPS-BUMP-1 merge. Rule 13 fails, so no Approvals and no tag. **Decision:** fixer r6 (wf_fd885c90-962: a fixer and a read-only checker) removes this x64 cost and keeps the bytecode forward. **Cause:** the cold body decoded the callee, the receiver and the Call slot and tested the callee before the receiver; LLVM put every operand that a later path uses before the first branch. So each cold host call with a receiver that is not a FUNCTION ran 48 instructions, against 26 at 057df9c2. **Fix** c6895b09 (`interp/ops.rs` only, x86-64 `cfg` only): the cold body tests the receiver first; it reads the callee at its fixed place (`fixed_callee`) only for a FUNCTION receiver; a new `#[cold]` `record_call_out` takes the record-window call and a prefixed call; `forward_or_call` takes 4 register arguments (was 6). | M8-P5-D5 | (2026-11-15; M6-ORCH-366, -678; plan v13 §18.1 row 143) **TA-EXTBYTES-ADMIT: the gap stays after the TA merge.** The facts are at 8c5b43e6, in `crates/ep9_heap/src/heap.rs`. External bytes (the off-heap ArrayBuffer and SharedArrayBuffer stores) drive only the GC trigger. `add_external_bytes` (:2865-2892) runs a major GC when the count would pass the trigger bound (:2883-2885). Then it adds the bytes and returns `Ok`. It fails only on an overflow of the count (`AllocError::TooLarge`). The bound counts against `max_heap_bytes` (`external_limit`, :2912-2932), but only to set the trigger. The doc says: "The add never fails for the heap limit, which bounds only the heap's own commits (H23)" (:2856-2857; also :2827-2828). So a huge off-heap ArrayBuffer is not admitted against `max_heap_bytes`. Its size caps are the VM caps of design 2.3 (a RangeError). H23 (Frozen part "rules") does not change for this point: from 585c9e0e to 8c5b43e6 the TA rows of H23 are cite moves and the `Atomics.wait` termination fill only. An admission check needs H23 rule text (G8). | M8-P5-D13 | (2026-11-15; M6-ORCH-601, -678) **TA-WAITASYNC-ORDER: ep9 keeps the node/V8 host-task order. This row closes the route at the TA merge.** ep9 resolves a notified `Atomics.waitAsync` waiter at the next job boundary. A notify, from the same agent too, only puts the waiter id into the agent's inbox. The spec (NotifyWaiter) resolves a same-agent waiter inside `Atomics.notify`. V8 posts a task for every waiter, of the same agent too. So ep9 matches the spec on trace S1 and node on traces S2 and S3. The in-tree doc of this order, with the 3-trace table, is `crates/ep9_vm/src/abi/typed.rs:578-592` at 8c5b43e6 (the doc of `queue_head_after_async_waiters`, :593). test262 d53ebc8b has no order test. (2) The RX1 tables (`gen-tables.py`, `gen-sets.py`): **UCD 17.0.0** (`UCD_VERSION = "17.0.0"`). (3) RX0, the regress fork (pin aae35dee): case data **Unicode 17.0** (`src/unicode.rs` of the synced checkout). (4) Rust std 1.99.1: **17.0.0** (`char::UNICODE_VERSION`). (5) The ICU4X 2.4.0 data (`icu_casemap`, `icu_properties_data`): **Unicode 18.0.0** (the data crate README: "generated with CLDR version 49.0.0, Unicode version 18.0.0"); H26 still says "ICU4X 2.3". (6) The test262 pin d53ebc8b: the property-escape files are **Unicode v17.0.0** (the header of `test/built-ins/RegExp/property-escapes/generated/ID_Start.js`), and the identifier tests go up to `start-unicode-17.0.0`. (7) tsrs (its own workspace): `unicode-id-start =1.1.2`, Unicode 15.1; it never reaches the engine. **Correction of M8-END-D5:** that row says that the 1.5.0 table "marks an unassigned code point range as ID_Start" and that "the front end is wrong". The range U+3D000..U+3FC3F (11,328 code points) is ID_Start in two separate Unicode 18 tables (`unicode-id-start` 1.5.0 and `unicode-ident` 1.0.27), and Unicode 18.0 adds a script of exactly 11,328 characters (derived from the count; the range is not read from a UCD file). So the crash cause is the version mix: the front end follows Unicode 18, while RX1, RX0, std, node and the test262 pin follow 17. The crate is not wrong, and "the crate fix goes with DEPS-BUMP-2" does not apply: no `unicode-id-start` release newer than 1.5.0 exists (crates.io, read 2026-11-16 for RBR14). The front end (oxc_regular_expression 0.158.0, unicode-id-start 1.5.0, Unicode 18.0.0) and RX1 (unicode_tables.rs, UCD 17.0.0) have different ID tables. 12,860 code points in 38 ranges are ID_Continue for the front end and not for RX1. 12,823 of them, in 27 ranges, are also ID_Start. U+3D000..U+3FC3F is 11,328 of them. There are 0 the other way. Form: a reviewed const list KNOWN_ID_DIFFERENCE (38 ranges), made from a probe of every code point U+0080..U+10FFFF with the real ep9_frontend and ep9_rx1. The probe set is equal to the table difference. id_differs (both parsers asked, as the first and as a later name character, with u) stays the detector. It returns false for ASCII, surrogates and values above U+10FFFF before it reads its cache, and the cache is two fixed bitsets of 0x110000 bits (278,528 bytes) (fixer r4). Check 1 compares validity first. It skips a text only when the front end accepts it, RX1 refuses it with InvalidCaptureGroupName (fixer r4), and the RX1 error position (a UTF-16 unit index) is inside a group name that holds a code point of the list (fixer r5). It decodes that code point raw, as \u{..} (hex digits only; a sign is refused), as \uHHHH or as a \uHHHH\uHHHH pair. A listed code point in a literal or a class is compared, and an RX1 InvalidCaptureGroupName at another name gives no skip. Checks 2 and 3 still run; the check 2 `v` exemption needs an RX1 accept, so it does not overlap the skip. A disagreement outside the list panics with "new front-end/RX1 identifier difference at U+XXXX". At fuzz_target! init, a sample check (the first, middle and last code point of each range differ; the code point before and after each range does not) stops a run with a stale list. Make the list again after an oxc or RX1 Unicode update (RX1 to Unicode 18: M2-exit G8). No H26 Decided sentence, Rules row or dep-guards check (2) result changes, so G8 stays 0. Writer: the M9-P1 integration fixer, by 2 named map rows. ## 20. M2 month 4 (month 10)

M2 is "Interpreter parity (hard gate; unchanged)" (docs/plan/09-milestones.md:101-113). Month 10 is M2 month 4. Its phases are M10-P0 to M10-P5: "M10-Pn" means month 10, phase n, and the milestone M10 is always written "milestone M10". Month 10 is not the planned M2-exit month; month 11 is, with a pre-registered switch (M10-PLAN-D1). §20.1 is the plan and the M10 pre-step. The next sections are "M10-P0 as built" to "M10-P5 as built" and "Month end".

| M10-PRE-DEADLDAR-KIND | (2026-11-19; plan v15 §2 step 8, §3.5; V15-D8; rule 69) **The DEAD-LDAR kind: a rewrite of the Frozen H24 R4 check; G8 +1 only if the probe meets its kill line.** DEAD-LDAR does not emit a binding `Ldar` whose next instruction writes the accumulator with no read and no label between. (1) REGOPT rule O2 says "Every load from a binding register (`Ldar` or `Mov` from a parameter or a named local) is emitted", for H24 R4 "no binding folds" (crates/ep9_frontend/src/bytecodegen/regopt.rs:20). (2) H24 R4 is a Rules row of a Frozen part: "BytecodeGen never folds a binding: each read of a `let`, `const`, `var` or parameter loads the binding" (H24:31); its check row names the bytecodegen goldens (H24:43). H24 rules are Frozen since M1 exit. (3) The R4 check is the REGOPT guard: `regopt_differences` (crates/ep9_frontend/src/bytecodegen/tests.rs:797-801) reports "a binding load is gone (H24 R4)" for each binding load that the optimized unit drops (the loop at tests.rs:826-837, the push at :835); the release corpus run calls it on every test262 unit (crates/ep9_frontend/src/bytecodegen/corpus.rs:254-266; the CI step "bytecodegen corpus digest (release)", ci.yml:492-500). (4) After DEAD-LDAR the guard accepts an elided dead binding load that it rejects today, and the H24 R4 text "each read ... loads the binding" changes (in `a, b` the dead `Ldar a` has no later read). By AR:76 "a check now accepts what it rejected" is a rewrite (AR:74 clarify and AR:75 fill do not fit: code and check results change, and H24 has no Open question on folds). G8 counts it (AR:80). **So:** the role takes the AR §3.2 rewrite approval set; the guard changes in place (tests.rs:826-837, line-neutral) with a new negative test; corpus.rs needs no edit. G8 +1 is spent only if the probe meets x64 TS Ir ≤ -1.0%; below the line: a DL row, no merge, no G8 | Plan v15 rule 69 pre-registers this rewrite; a disputed kind is a rewrite (README §3.3) | crates/ep9_frontend/src/bytecodegen/regopt.rs:20; crates/ep9_frontend/src/bytecodegen/tests.rs:797-801, :826-837, :835; crates/ep9_frontend/src/bytecodegen/corpus.rs:254-266; .github/workflows/ci.yml:492-500; docs/adr/H24-debug-and-profiling-hooks.md:31, :43; docs/adr/README.md:74-76, :80; plan v15 §1 rule 69, §3.5; M10-PLAN-D8 |
| M10-PRE-NAMED-MISS-READ | (2026-11-19; plan v15 §2 step 9 (b), §10 Q1; V15-D6; M6-ORCH-1026) **The named IC misses of octane-typescript: one class holds 95.47%; the Q1 condition holds; more POLY_CASES does not help.** Mac aarch64, an `ic-stats` release build at 86e39c65 with a local per-site counter (not committed), the TS workload N = 5. Named misses 41,417,567 (load 29,282,699 of 357,994,202 visits = 8.18%; store 12,134,868 of 68,184,318 = 17.80%). Megamorphic sites hold 97.82%: the stub cache hit in the cold body (no runtime call) is 95.47% (load 29.13 M, store 10.41 M); a stub hit whose add needs SLOTS growth 1.90% (runtime call); a stub cache miss 0.45%. Sites with ≤ 4 shapes have 0 misses; sites with ≥ 33 shapes 70.47%. 50% of the misses are in 26 sites; `nodeType` loads alone are 43.19%. Cause: the TS compiler AST class tree (about 42 subclasses, each with its own root shape) goes through the shared `AST` / `ASTSpan` constructors and walkers. Check: the per-site sums equal the built-in `ic-stats` totals; a second run gives the same megamorphic counts. **Conclusions:** the Q1 condition (one class ≥ 25%) holds; an IC list append (more `POLY_CASES`, ic.rs:135) cuts about 0%; the class needs a cheaper megamorphic path (a stub cache probe in the fast body on the MEGA branch only), which is not an IC list append, so its G8 kind (H15, H16) is open and the LEVER-12 W-pre reads it first. Limits: visits, not time; aarch64 only | Plan v15 V15-D6 (measure first) and §10 Q1 | crates/ep9_vm/src/ic.rs:135; plan v15 §2 step 9 (b), §10; M6-ORCH-1026 |
| M10-PRE-WIDE-READ | (2026-11-19; plan v15 §2 step 9 (c), §10 Q2; V15-D6; M6-ORCH-1026) **The prefixed instructions of TS: the feedback slot and the forward jump offset overflow, never a register.** 0 compile: `--print-bytecode` of the GW11b jitless binary at 86e39c65 (the jit binary and the m8-p5 binary give the same dump). Static: 5,786 of 125,281 instructions are prefixed (4.62%; Wide 5,777, ExtraWide 9); the operand that overflows is the feedback slot 85.9%, the jump offset 12.3%, a constant 1.2%, an immediate 0.7%, a register 0. Executed (estimate from V8 block coverage of the same file): 32.3 M of 1,621 M (1.99%); the x86-64 cachegrind count of the same bytecode is 39.2 M, so the jump class is about 21 M (the estimate under-counts it by about 7 M) and the slot class about 18.4 M. GetNamedProperty.Wide is 10.27 M (it matches cachegrind). 6 functions hold 75% of the executed prefixed instructions (scanner, parser, emitter, type flow). **Conclusions:** the Q2 condition (the read names the operand) holds; no static slot order beats the source order (reverse, loop-first and kind-first are worse); only a profile order or a format change moves the slot class; a branch island (`JumpIf<inverse> +short` over `Jump.Wide`) removes est. 5.5-6.7 M prefixed runs at 180-438 sites (a low bound). ## 21. M2 month 5 (month 11)

M2 is "Interpreter parity (hard gate; unchanged)" (docs/plan/09-milestones.md:101-113). Month 11 is M2 month 5. Its phases are M11-P0 to M11-P3, one lever set each (plan v16 rule 98): "M11-Pn" means month 11, phase n, and the milestone M11 is always written "milestone M11". Rows: octane-typescript (the decision row) and the guard rows t0-branchy, deltablue, raytrace, richards. Counters: wall, cycles, instructions, branch misses, L1i misses (the LAYOUT-PIN perf list). **Pair:** One read round on one box: wall of arm 1 / wall of arm 0; same build, row and round. No second retry: if the 3-box result is not MERGE, the lever closes with the result as measured. **Guard rows:** A guard row with a pooled wall median above 1.010 is **GUARD-FAIL**: no merge and no G8 in month 11; the lever closes as measured. No second fix is allowed: a STOP from now on moves the A/B to M12-P0.** FIRST READ (probe code head cdd13fa7c936e81e3bdb63a30f9f3ca98287603d; bench head 78c726c0632ab861be9b0fb58b82036d44b9f64f on branch `m2m11/p3-star-dst-bench` = the code head + the bench-only change that makes arm 2 the default; base 0814321a; cachegrind Ir; one CI run reads base and head): run 45038956693 (octane-typescript): linux-x64 jit 53,091,125,887 -> 52,573,012,796 = -0.976%, jitless 52,480,794,957 -> 51,960,304,803 = -0.992%, against the line "x64 TS Ir falls by ≥ 1.0% in both builds": NOT MET (short by 0.024 and 0.008 points); linux-arm64 -1.504% / -1.520%. Run 45038939520 (BENCH-SET, 19 rows jit, 12 rows jitless): no row above +0.5% on either arch (x64 worst +0.000%, arm64 worst +0.001%); t0-prop x64 -0.706% / -0.712%, arm64 -1.444% / -1.465%: these 2 parts are met. THE NAMED DEFECT (the per-function cachegrind rows of run 45038956693, x64 jitless, and the x86-64 Linux disassembly of cdd13fa7): `ep9h__ics__tail__GetNamedPropertyStar` 12,664,967,303 Ir over 221,865,564 runs = 57.08 per run; the plain named load of the same pairs (base - head of `ep9h__ics__tail__GetNamedProperty`) 11,166,990,281 Ir = 50.33 per run; `Star` 8.00 per run; so a fused named pair saved 8 + 50.33 - 57.08 = 1.25 instructions, not about 3 (each fused context form saves 3). The cause: the IC hit shapes join in one exit block. The exit of the plain handler is 3 instructions, and LLVM copies it into each hit path (4 hit exits, br=5). The fused exit was 9 instructions (the late dst read, lea, test, cmov, the store, a dispatch of 4), and LLVM copies only a tail of 4 instructions or less (the LLVM default `tail-dup-placement-aggressive-threshold` = 4, read in the LLVM source, not measured). So each fused hit paid a jump to one shared 9-instruction exit and a lea / mov pair for the new pc: plain + 7 on the field and length hits, plain + 6 on the prototype hits (br=2). THE ONE FIX: commit 0d3fd5cbc15814df4fb98333ce7f855650574194 (signed; parent cdd13fa7; `crates/ep9_vm/src/interp/ops.rs` only, 86 insertions, 1 deletion): on x86-64 the hit exit decodes the late dst with a branch on its sign (the aarch64 form of `R::of_out_operand`; the negative arm is cold). The shared exit is 7 instructions; a field or length hit runs plain + 5, a prototype hit plain + 4. Other targets keep `dsl::star_dst`, so the aarch64 code does not change. No bytecode, opcode, golden, frames file or other handler byte changes (the checker compared 572 `ep9h__` symbols of the x86-64 Linux build: only ics and sib GetNamedPropertyStar differ). A new test compares the branch form with `dsl::star_dst` for all 256 one-byte dst values and at Wide scale. SECOND READ (code head 0d3fd5cb; bench head 404fcf3738453eaf098603ad0047b7e4a310fdee on branch `m2m11/p3-star-dst-bench-2` = the fix + the same bench-only change; base 0814321a): run 45045711563 (octane-typescript): linux-x64 jit 53,091,238,587 -> 52,129,373,911 = -1.812%, jitless 52,481,194,342 -> 51,516,738,817 = -1.838%: MET (the static estimate of the fix check was -1.811% / -1.837%); the fused named load is now 12,221,460,839 Ir = 55.08 per run, a saving of 3.25 per pair; linux-arm64 -1.499% / -1.522% (the fix does not change aarch64). Run 45045725699 (BENCH-SET, 19 rows jit, 12 rows jitless): no row above +0.5% on either arch (worst +0.000%); t0-prop x64 -1.884% / -1.900%, arm64 -1.444% / -1.464%: MET. K-2 on the fixed head: the dumps of arms unset, 0, 1 and 2 are byte-equal to the dumps of the first head (lines 2 to the end of the arm-0 dump have the registered sha256 fd064829...af73aa): MET by identity. K-3 on the fixed head: the linux-x64 cross `-v` log gives `insns` 162 for `ep9h__ics__tail__GetNamedPropertyStar` ≤ 160 + 8; no frames file changed; `--expect 290` PASS; the native SIDECI disasm jobs on 4 targets PASS (row M11-P3-L16-PREREG-FILL): MET. A REPORT COLUMN, NOT A LINE: the simulated indirect-branch mispredicts (cachegrind Bim, x64): first read -10.072% jit / -11.206% jitless; second read -2.892% jit / -12.406% jitless (the jit build lost most of its fall); a branch cost shows in the wall-time A/B, not here; a note for the A/B read and for the JIT reviewer of a merge. THE FIX CHECK (verdict ship; findings (c), no change): F1 the fused handler has 3 indirect jumps (one shared hit dispatch, a cold negative-dst dispatch, the cold jump), the plain handler 5. The exit shape of the plain handler is not reachable without a K-3 break: an early dst decode makes the handler save rbx at entry (`frame=entry`, a new frames saves row = a K-3 STOP), and one exit per hit shape needs code in `ic.rs`, outside the grants. Before the fix the shared hit dispatch mispredicted on 78% of its runs in the simulated count (the plain handler: 51%). F2 the windows-x64 GetNamedPropertyStar grows 163 -> 181 instructions (br 1 -> 2); the registered K-3 (c) line reads the linux log only; this is a merge item for the H15 rule-81 rows. A TEXT FIX OF THE PROBE ROLE (probe role check, finding 1): the message of cdd13fa7 and the role report say that the 18 `fuzz/seeds/unit_loader` seeds change "by the ABI number"; that is not true. The base seeds were stale: they held bytecode from before LDAR-ELIDE (the seeds test checks versions and digests, not a fresh compile). So the bless also wrote the LDAR-ELIDE arm-0 bytecode of 0814321a (for example one function body 18 -> 14 bytes, 2 dead `Ldar` removed). No fused opcode is in the seeds. The behavior is correct; only the text is wrong; no amend; the merge part re-blesses the seeds | K-4 is a registered kill line: a miss is a STOP with no box and one DL row, and no pass by explanation. M11-P3-PICK allows the role one fix of the named defect, then each kill line is read again on the new head. The fix removes only the 2 extra exit instructions; it changes no bytecode and no handler other than the fused named one; the second read meets K-4 by about 0.8 points in both builds. ### 21.8 M11-P3: the STAR-DST merge (appended after 21.7: the file order is the landing order)

**Result.** The merge line `m2m11/p3-star-dst-merge` holds the set of the A/B word MERGE (M11-P3-L16-VERDICT): 3 fused opcodes (GetNamedPropertyStar, LdaCurrentContextSlotStar and LdaContextSlotStar at 0x9e-0xa0; each does a load and then stores the result to a register, and the destination register is the last operand), 290 handlers and bytecode ABI 7. The set is the only optimized form, and the switch `EP9_STAR_DST` is gone. The corpus digest moves to `f199320e…cb3d` over 94,783 units, read on 4 targets (BCG-CORPUS-20). Codex ran 2 rounds on the phase range. In round 1 the Codex content filter stopped the code slice 2 times, so a Claude adversarial reviewer read the interpreter slice in the place of Codex. The items of sort (a) and (b) are fixed in 9 signed commits (one more is closed by the digest commit), the items of sort (c) are routes, and the loop stops after round 2 by the orchestrator decision M6-ORCH-1393 (M11-P3-CODEX). G8 is +3 at this merge (H02 ABI core, H16 feedback core, H15 dispatch core), so the month-11 G8 count is +5 of the cap +5 (M11-P3-MERGE). On the merge head the code CI, BENCH-SET and the TS row are green, except the expected adr-lint gap of the owed review sets, and the TS row repeats the K-4 second read of the probe.

### 22.1 The plan rows

Plan v17 was accepted on 2026-11-24 at 06:48 +0800, after 2 audits and one fix round (M6-ORCH-1445). ### 22.2 The pre-registration rows (written before any month-12 box)

**Result.** Five rule-96 rows of plan v17 §3 step 4: M12-PRE-AB93, M12-PRE-G8, M12-PRE-SWITCH, M12-PRE-MONTH13 and M12-PRE-TD3. Each row is signed and pushed on the docs side branch `m2m12/prereg` before the first month-12 box (the TD-3 box); its sha is the PREREG_REF that the box script checks. No line of a row is re-worded after its first box.

| ID | Decision | Reason | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| M12-PRE-AB93 | (2026-11-24; pre-registration; rule 96; plan v17 §2 rules 13, 93, 96, 101, §2.2, §4.2, §4.3, §8.2; V17-D8, V17-D10; the month-11 form M11-PRE-AB93) **Rule 93 in month 12: the pooled x86 time A/B, written once, before the first month-12 lever box, so no data can move a line.** It is the one form for the lever reads of month 12: GC-BUDGET (wave 2, row M12-P1-GC-PREREG), WIDE-SET (wave 3, row M12-P2-WIDE-PREREG) and LEVER-19 (wave 5, its own row). **Flow:** the DL pre-registration row of the lever (rule 96) ─► 2 boxes at once, each builds on the box ─► 1 warm round + 31 read rounds ─► pool the 62 pairs ─► read ONCE ─► MERGE (the merge role ─► merge-head CI ─► tag ─► G8 spent at the merge), or KILL (one DL row; no merge, no G8, no tag; the branch stays), or else 1 more box ─► read ONCE on 93 pairs ─► MERGE, or closed as measured. **Arms:** arm 0 = the base value; the decision arm = the lever (GC-BUDGET: B1; WIDE-SET: S = value 3). A part arm runs only when the part has its own G8 row or its own registered value (WIDE-SET: W1 = value 1 and W2 = value 2; GC-BUDGET: B2). No trim arm. Arm 0' (the A/A arm) runs on box 1 of the first same-binary lever read of the month only: GC-BUDGET, or WIDE-SET if GC-BUDGET is NOT RUN; its cost (about 0.15 box-h) is inside the 1.3-2.0 box-h of that read. **Same-binary form** (a run-time switch read once per process: `EP9_GC_BUDGET`, `EP9_WIDE_FORMS`): all arms are one binary; the run log records the equal sha256 and the switch value of each run. **Two-binary form** (only for a lever with no switch): both arms are built on the box from one base sha. **Layout forms:** every row runs in the aligned form (`-C llvm-args=-align-all-functions=6`, the shipped x86-64 build since m11-p1); the default form (`RUSTFLAGS=` empty) runs the octane-typescript jitless row only. **Builds, rows, counters:** both builds (jit and jitless); octane-typescript (the decision row) and the guard rows t0-branchy, deltablue, raytrace, richards; wall, cycles, instructions, branch misses, L1i misses. **Pair:** one read round on one box: wall of the lever arm / wall of arm 0; same build, row and round. A pair with a failed run or a busy guard is dropped; the summary prints n. **Statistic:** the median of the pooled pairs, with the order-statistic 95% interval (no distribution model): the sorted pairs 23 and 40 for n = 62; 10 and 22 for n = 31; 37 and 57 for n = 93. For a smaller n: the sorted pairs k and n - k + 1, k the largest with P(Bin(n, 1/2) <= k - 1) <= 0.025; the summary prints n and the ranks. **Decision cell:** octane-typescript, jitless build, wall, aligned form. **MERGE:** the decision cell median <= 0.990 and its interval wholly below 1.000; and the cycles cell (same pairs) median <= 0.990; and each box alone has a decision-cell median below 1.000; and the jit TS wall cell median <= 1.000; and the default-form TS jitless median <= 1.000, else the result is one more box. **KILL:** the decision cell median > 0.990 and its interval wholly above 0.980 (the data exclude a 2% gain), on the TS jitless cell in both layout forms; if only one form reads KILL and the MERGE lines do not all hold, the result is one more box and the DL row says "a layout draw is not excluded". **One more box:** any other result. 1 more box; every line is read once on the 3 boxes pooled (93 pairs). No second retry: a 3-box result that is not MERGE closes the lever as measured. **Guard rows:** each guard row is read in both builds; a guard row with a pooled wall median above 1.010 is GUARD-FAIL: no merge and no G8 in month 12; the lever closes as measured. A narrowed form is a new lever set with its own rule-96 row. **Two-binary support line:** the instructions cell must move as the probe's x64 Ir read says (half of the read or more); else the read is VOID: the summary prints only the VOID cause and the instructions cell; one rerun box; a second VOID closes the lever as "no read". **A/A sanity:** if the box-1 A/A pairs (arm 0' / arm 0, n = 31, sorted pairs 10 and 22) give an interval that does not hold 1.000, the read is VOID (harness bias): fix the harness, one rerun box, read once. Each VOID or lost box counts against the 15.9 box-h cap (rules 94, 102). **Own values:** a lever row may set other values only before its first box, with the reason. It may not drop a line. One named exception: the GC-BUDGET row replaces the cycles line by a report cell and adds the splay and memory guards of plan v17 §4.2 (splay and octane-splay pooled median <= 1.000, hard; the peak RSS of every MEMREAD row against `node --jitless` <= 0.95 and against `d8 --jitless` <= 1.50); it keeps all 4 guard rows. **Verdict words:** MERGE, KILL, ONE MORE BOX, GUARD-FAIL, VOID; after the 3-box read a result that is not MERGE closes the lever as measured. Each lever row states the order of the words before its first box. The read step prints the row id of its pre-registration row. **What is read once:** the pooled statistic, after both boxes end. No look at one box alone before the pool; no added rounds; no changed row list. The summary script prints the verdict word; the orchestrator copies it. No DL text written after the data releases a merge (rule 96). **Rule 13 cap:** a lever that passes rule 93 may raise Ir on a row by at most +1.0%; Ir is never a merge reason for a hot-handler or bytecode-shape lever. **G8:** spent at the merge only, after MERGE (M12-PRE-G8). **Cost (est.):** 1.3-2.0 box-h per 2-box read by the arm count; one more box 0.7-0.9. **What it does not say:** the A/B number is the gain of the lever shape, not the gate move (rule 101). The transfer is read once, at the end Path B, pooled over the merged sets, with its band (M12-PRE-MONTH13). **What a result changes:** MERGE lets the lever merge, take its tag and spend its G8 row. KILL, GUARD-FAIL or a read closed as measured frees the G8 row of the set (a later pick uses it only by a SWAP row, M12-PRE-G8); box-h already spent stay spent. The GC-BUDGET decision-arm median is an input of line 1 of M12-PRE-MONTH13. No line of this row is re-worded after the first lever box: a line set after the data is a moved goal post. | Plan v17 changes 3 parts of M11-PRE-AB93 and keeps the rest. DECISION CELL: octane-typescript, jitless build, wall, aligned form, arm S / arm 0. **MERGE** (M12-PRE-AB93): the decision cell median <= 0.990 and its interval wholly below 1.000; and the cycles cell (same pairs) median <= 0.990; and each box alone has a decision-cell median below 1.000; and the jit TS wall cell median <= 1.000; and the default-form TS jitless median <= 1.000, else the result is one more box. **KILL** (M12-PRE-AB93): the decision cell median > 0.990 and its interval wholly above 0.980 (the data exclude a 2% gain), on the TS jitless cell in both layout forms; if only one form reads KILL and the MERGE lines do not all hold, the result is one more box and the DL row says "a layout draw is not excluded"; in a 3-box read a KILL in one form only reads CLOSED AS MEASURED with the same words. **ONE MORE BOX** (M12-PRE-AB93): any other result: box ep9-x86-m12-wide-3; every line is read once on the 3 boxes pooled (93 pairs); no second retry: a 3-box result that is not MERGE closes the lever as measured. **GUARD-FAIL** (M12-PRE-AB93): each guard row is read in both builds (aligned form, arm S / arm 0); a guard row with a pooled wall median above 1.010 is GUARD-FAIL: no merge and no G8 in month 12; the lever closes as measured; a narrowed form is a new lever set with its own rule-96 row. Every guard row keeps this line (M12-PRE-AB93 names no exception for this set). **VOID**: (1) A/A (M12-PRE-AB93; only when arm 0' runs): the box-1 A/A cell (octane-typescript, jitless, aligned form, wall, arm 0' / arm 0, n = 31, sorted pairs 10 and 22) has an interval that does not hold 1.000 (harness bias): fix the harness, one rerun box, read once; (2) OWN support line (the design §7 "switch sanity" in the M11-P3-L16-PREREG OV-5 form; M12-PRE-AB93 writes this line for the two-binary form only): in each build, the pooled TS instructions median of arm S / arm 0 (aligned form) is at or below the support value of that build, and its interval is wholly below 1.000; the support value = 1 - half of the x64 TS Ir fall of that build in the bench run of BENCH_HEAD against the base, in % (so 1 - fall / 200), to 4 places (at a tie in the 5th place both values pass); if the bench run reads no fall in a build, that build keeps the interval part only; FILL: the 2 falls and the 2 support values; else VOID ("the switch did not act"); reason: a prefixed instruction runs more instructions than its 1-byte form (est. 20-30), so the cell must fall when the forms are in use; it is not a gain line; (3) a box check fails (a STOP, a build or freshness line, a layout line, a binary sha256 that differs between arms, the unset / arm-0 dump check). On a VOID the summary prints only the VOID cause and the instructions cells. ONE retry or rerun box for the row (ep9-x86-m12-wide-3): a VOID rerun box takes the retry place and the place of the VOID box (box 1 for a pooled cause, with the arms of box 1), and the read is once more on 2 boxes; a second VOID closes the lever NO READ; after a VOID rerun, a result ONE MORE BOX closes the lever NO READ. A retry or rerun box starts only if the cut order of plan v17 §8.2 leaves room under the 15.9 box-h cap, by one DL row before that box; else cut step 5 closes the lever "no read". **PART RULE** (plan v17 §4.3; OWN where the design §7 adds), read once, only after a MERGE of arm S: for P in {W-1, W-2}, Q = the arm without P (W2 for P = W-1, W1 for P = W-2); part P joins the merge if the pooled TS jitless cycles median of arm S / Q is <= 0.997 (aligned form; the summary prints the interval next to it, and the verdict row says "part split by median only"); if one part fails, the other merges alone only if its own arm (W1 or W2 against arm 0) passes the MERGE lines and has no GUARD-FAIL; OWN: if that does not hold, or both parts fail the line, the set merges whole and the DL row says "part split not resolved". Reason for 0.997 (the design): a gain of 0.3% is under the low end of the est. gain of the smaller part (W-2, 0.4%); rule 98 reads the set, so the part rule can only save a G8 row, never block a MERGE. A part arm gives no merge when arm S is not MERGE. PARTS words: W-1 + W-2, W-1 ALONE, W-2 ALONE, SET (part split not resolved). REPORT CELLS (no line): W1 / arm 0 and W2 / arm 0 for every row and build; the L1i-miss and branch-miss cells of each arm; the A/A width. WORD ORDER (the first word that applies prints): VOID (NO READ on a second VOID), GUARD-FAIL, MERGE (then the PARTS word), KILL, ONE MORE BOX; in a 3-box read ONE MORE BOX reads CLOSED AS MEASURED. READ ONCE: one script reads the pooled statistic once, after both boxes ended and were destroyed; the sha256 of the read code is recorded at each box start, and the read refuses a box when that code changed after it; no look at one box alone (the box summary has no ratio); no added rounds; no changed row list; the read prints the row id M12-P2-WIDE-PREREG and the verdict word; the orchestrator copies the word into M12-P2-WIDE-VERDICT; no DL text written after the data releases a merge (rule 96). RULE 13 (M12-PRE-AB93): the merged arm may raise Ir on a row by at most +1.0%; Ir is never a merge reason for this lever (FILL: the worst BENCH-SET row per arch and build of the bench run). LOST OR LATE BOX (rules 94, 102): at +100 min with no end line the orchestrator reads the step file of the box; at +110 min it destroys the box; the hard timer of the box set (FILL, at most 110 min) can destroy it first; a lost box is a record and counts against the cap (priced 2.7 box-h, plan v17 §8.2 row 9); OWN: it takes the rerun place as a VOID box does (plan v17 §8.2 row 9 prices a lost box with one rerun). CAP: est. 1.6-2.0 box-h for the 2 boxes (plan v17 §8.2 row 3), one more box est. 0.8-0.9 (row 3b); the cap 15.9 box-h outside an exit batch is not raised; the boxes start only if the hold rule of plan v17 §8.2 holds (spent + the high value + its retry + 5.88 <= 15.9), OWN: at the box set's own high values when they are larger (the STAR-DST box-set check gave est. 2.24-2.37 box-h for its 2 boxes, above the row 3 value); FILL: the per-box hard timer and the estimate of the box-set check, the box-h spent in month 12 before box 1, and the room. no trim arm; arm 0' (the A/A arm) runs on box 1 of the first same-binary lever read of the month (GC-BUDGET, the first read, O8). **Same-binary form** (a run-time switch read once per process): all arms are one binary; the run log records the equal sha256 and the switch value of each run. **Two-binary form** (only for a lever with no switch): both arms are built on the box from one base sha. **Layout forms:** every row runs in the aligned form (`-C llvm-args=-align-all-functions=6`); the default form (`RUSTFLAGS=` empty) runs the octane-typescript jitless row only. **Builds, rows, counters:** both builds (jit and jitless); octane-typescript (the decision row) and the guard rows t0-branchy, deltablue, raytrace, richards; a lever row adds a guard row only with a named mechanism; wall, cycles, instructions, branch misses, L1i misses. **Pair:** one read round on one box: the lever arm / arm 0, same build, row, form and round; a pair with a failed run or a busy guard is dropped; the summary prints n. **Statistic:** the median of the pooled pairs, with the order-statistic 95% interval (no distribution model): the sorted pairs 23 and 40 for n = 62; 10 and 22 for n = 31; 37 and 57 for n = 93; for a smaller n, the sorted pairs k and n - k + 1, k the largest with P(Bin(n, 1/2) <= k - 1) <= 0.025; the summary prints n and the ranks. **Decision cell:** octane-typescript, jitless build, wall, aligned form, the decision arm / arm 0. **MERGE:** (M1) the decision cell median <= 0.990 and (M2) its interval wholly below 1.000; and (M3) the cycles cell (same pairs) median <= 0.990; and (M4) each box alone has a decision-cell median below 1.000; and (M5) the jit TS wall cell median <= 1.000; and (M6) the default-form TS jitless median <= 1.000; **and no LEVER cell is WEAK** (new); else the result is one more box. **KILL:** the decision cell median > 0.990 and its interval wholly above 0.980, on the TS jitless cell in both layout forms; if only one form reads KILL and the MERGE lines do not all hold, the result is one more box and the DL row says "a layout draw is not excluded"; in a 3-box read a KILL in one form only reads CLOSED AS MEASURED. **VOID:** (1) A/A: the box-1 A/A cell (octane-typescript, jitless, aligned, wall, arm 0' / arm 0, n = 31, sorted pairs 10 and 22) has an interval that does not hold 1.000 (harness bias): fix the harness, one rerun box, read once; (2) support: in the two-binary form the instructions cell moves as the probe's x64 Ir read says (half of the read or more); in the same-binary form the switch line of the lever row; (3) a box check fails. On a VOID the summary prints only the cause and the count cells. One rerun box; a second VOID closes the lever NO READ; after a VOID rerun, a result ONE MORE BOX closes the lever NO READ. Each VOID or lost box counts against the 15.9 box-h cap (rules 94, 102). **ONE MORE BOX:** any other result; it includes the case "every MERGE line holds and a LEVER cell is WEAK". 1 more box; every line is read once on the 3 boxes pooled (93 pairs). | M13-END-D8 | (2026-11-25 to -26; rules 56, 82, 94, 104; the user rules on compiling agents, sync scripts and shas; M6-ORCH-1549, -1553, -1556, -1561, -1569, -1585, -1586, -1599, -1601, -1602, -1603, -1607, -1609, -1618, -1627, -1631, -1638) **The lessons of month 13, each with its source. Each is a process fact for plan v19; none moves a month-13 word.** (1) **A name that does not resolve is a retry, not a box fault:** the FUZZ-H script refused twice when the Worker host name did not resolve on the Mac for about 4 min; no box was made, and the third start passed (M6-ORCH-1631). (2) **A push to the PR head cancels its pull_request run** (concurrency cancel-in-progress): no push to `m2/m13` before its PR run ends and the tag is made; a side head goes to its own ref first (M6-ORCH-1603). (3) **The detach check:** a start-path dry try under a `bash -c` wrapper stopped at the detach check (rc 1, "not detached"); the README form passed; no box was lost (M6-ORCH-1602). (4) **The rule-82 table check:** an unescaped pipe in the WIDE-FIX FILL row gave 5 cells against a 4-cell header; the push gate refused it, and the row was made again on a new branch with only the escape changed; a DL row writer runs the table check before it reports (adr-lint does not count cells) (M6-ORCH-1601). (5) **Never move a cargo target dir:** a moved target kept old CARGO_BIN_EXE paths (M6-ORCH-1549); every new worktree runs all 4 sync scripts, because the push gate builds (M6-ORCH-1561); a sha typed from memory made a failed dispatch, so each sha is read with `git rev-parse` first (M6-ORCH-1586). (6) **GitHub API limits:** 4 pollers at 60-90 s hit the rate limit; at most 2 pollers, each stopped when its run is read (M6-ORCH-1556); a watcher bug (`set -- $J` overwrote the run list) cost about 60 min on 4 run ends, with no wrong read (M6-ORCH-1569). (7) **Compile slots:** review lenses outside the pool slots could make 3 compiling agents for a short time; reviewers read only or take a pool slot (M6-ORCH-1553). (8) **A 1e-5 identity line meets the A/A noise:** 2 runs of the same B1 code differ by 1.80e-5 (jit octane-typescript Ir) and 1.12e-5 (jitless splay Ir), and the GC merge-head line read FAIL on 2 Ir rows (-1.41e-5, +1.34e-5); this noise was stated before the run, and the call was MERGE (M6-ORCH-1585, -1599; route AA-NOISE-1E5). ### 24.2 The pre-registration rows (written before any month-14 box; appended after 24.1: the file order is the landing order)

**Result.** The 4 month rows of plan v19 §3 (rows 1-4): M14-PRE-AB94 (form F1b, the rule of the band B, and tau of the 60 null cells), M14-PRE-G8 (the G8 cap), M14-PRE-SWITCH (the exit switch) and M14-PRE-MONTH15 (the direction lines of plan v20). Each row is written before the first box of month 14 (the SIMD x86 test box too) and pushed on the docs side branch `m2m14/prereg`; its commit is the PREREG_REF that the box script checks. A registered row is never re-worded: an as-built value goes in a later row (rule 96). Each row cites its month-13 form by id and by the sha256 of that row line (the whole line, from its first character to its last, with no newline) at dbc8a2aa. Every repo `file:line` and command is read at dbc8a2aa (the `m2/m13` head with §24.1); its code is the code of 0b710261 (tag m13-p1): `git diff --stat 0b710261 dbc8a2aa -- crates third_party Cargo.lock .cargo rust-toolchain.toml tools` prints nothing.

| ID | Decision | Reason | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| M14-PRE-AB94 | (2026-11-26; pre-registration; rules 13, 21, 93, 96, 104, 105, 111, 112, 117; plan v19 §2 rules 93, 104, 105, 112, 117, §2.2, §3 row 1; V19-D8, V19-D9, V19-D19 (M14-PLAN-D8, M14-PLAN-D9, M14-PLAN-D19); the month-13 form M13-PRE-AB93; M13-P1-GC-MERGE-CALL; M13-P1-GC-FILL; routes AB94-F1B, AA-BAND, AA-NOISE-1E5) **Rule 93 in month 14: form F1b = form F1 (M13-PRE-AB93) with the 6 changes below. It is written once, before the first box of month 14 (the SIMD x86 test box too), so no data can move a line. No MERGE, KILL, VOID, level or guard line of F1 changes.** **F1 is kept by reference:** every line of M13-PRE-AB93 holds in month 14, with "month 14" for "month 13", except the 6 changes. The AB93 row line has the sha256 ee76d742b16c36f9964b3a634e04ebc9b712ff17809e166b62732e47921377ed at dbc8a2aa. F1b is the one form for the lever reads of month 14: ALLOC-SET (M14-P1; row M14-P1-ALLOC-PREREG) and LEVER-21 (M14-P2; its own row after M14-P2-PICK). Each lever PREREG cites this row by id and by the sha256 of its line (computed the same way) and prints only its own values (rule 21). **CHANGE 1, PROOF (b) of an IDENTITY cell:** "the x64 Ir of the row in the bench run of the bench head against the base differs by at most 1e-5" becomes "differs by at most B" (abs(head / base - 1) <= B), B = the band of change 2. The rest of (b) is kept: (b) reads only when the bench row and the box row run the same workload text (equal sha256); a jitless octane row has no bench Ir row, so (b) has no reading there. **This overrides the AB93 line "The identity band is 1e-5"**, with a new fact (M13-P1-GC-MERGE-CALL; the 1.49e-5 and 1.76e-5 pairs are also the A/A same-sha noise of run 45606203565 in M13-P1-GC-FILL): 4 same-code Ir pairs of month 13 read 1.12e-5, 1.49e-5, 1.76e-5 and 1.80e-5, and the 2 merge-head rows that read FAIL read 1.34e-5 and 1.41e-5. All are above 1e-5, so the AB93 fact "the tool noise on 30 same-code cells is at most 8.7e-6" (run 45349037862) does not hold now. **What the band gives up:** B (est. about 5e-5, a guess; at most 1e-4) is above the smallest known lever action on a guard row (1.5e-5, richards under the WIDE-SET arm S), so (b) alone cannot tell that action from noise. PROOF (a) and (c) still catch it: an IDENTITY cell needs (a), (b) and (c) together; (c) needs a count run that shows that no handler, table entry or decision point that the lever changes runs on the row; a bytecode change fails (a); a lever whose changed surface cannot be named has no (c), so its cells are LEVER cells. **CHANGE 2, the band B (the formula is fixed here, before its data):** AA-BAND, 0 boxes: 5 bench-mode dispatches with base = head = tag m13-p1 (0b710261), x64, both builds. One dispatch gives 19 jit BENCH-SET rows, 12 jitless rows (the jitless leg has no octane rows) and octane-typescript in both builds (a separate TS-set dispatch) = 33 cells; **5 x 33 = 165 null Ir cells.** A null cell = abs(Ir head / Ir base - 1) of one row, in one build, in one dispatch. **B = 3 x the largest of the 165 cells. The cap:** if 3 x the largest is above 1e-4, then B = 1e-4, and each row and build with one of its 5 cells above 3.3e-5 (1e-4 / 3) has no Ir reading: PROOF (b) has no reading there, so its cell is a LEVER cell. B is read once, on all 165 cells: a failed dispatch runs again in the same form before the read, and no cell is dropped (own line of this row: a dropped cell can only make B smaller by chance). **The value of B is not in this row:** the AA-BAND read row (its own DL row; route AA-BAND) prints the 165 cells, the largest cell, B and the capped rows, and is pushed before the first box of month 14. The FILL kit gives B to each FILL writer (rule 112). **CHANGE 3, the merge-head clause of a PREREG:** "bench Ir within 1e-5 of the read head, else the merge stops" becomes 3 lines: (1) deterministic equality: the bytecode sha256 per row, the H0 GC trace sigs per row, the cell counts by kind and the facts dump are equal; (2) bench Ir: \|dIr - d\| <= B on every row, where d = the per-row Ir change of the merge-head draft (the arm switch removed) against arm S, read once by a 0-box bench before box 1 and printed in the FILL row; (3) the H1 GC counts agree within a band of +-1. A failed line stops the merge. Reason: the GC merge line read FAIL on noise on 3 of 40 rows (M13-P1-GC-MERGE-CALL); the removal of the switch tests (in `lookup_with`, the record hooks and the construct path) moves Ir by est. 1e-4 to 5e-4 of a row (a guess), more than B, so a line with no d would stop a valid MERGE. **CHANGE 4, a row on a SIMD body:** a row whose timed code runs a SIMD body of the lever (the source hash runs on every row) is a LEVER cell, unless `EP9_SIMD=` forces the same body on the box and in the bench. The x86 box prints the body of each SIMD table per read. Reason: cachegrind may not show SHA-NI or AVX-512 to the program (not verified; plan v19 risk K13), so the bench can run another body than the box. **CHANGE 5, ONE MORE BOX:** + rule 117: one more box is not bought when the 2-box data fix a MERGE line that a third box cannot change (M4: one box alone at or above 1.000). So the runner takes its default: `default_threads()` = `std::thread::available_parallelism()` (`tools/test262/src/main.rs:80-81` at 8386386e; ":57: --threads <n> worker processes (default: all CPUs)"), and on Linux that count reads the affinity mask (E: Rust std `sched_getaffinity`; R28 §3.1).
